faqs.question: What does GPSPL include under Video Technologies?
faqs.answer: GPSPL includes PTZ cameras, video conferencing cameras, lecture capture, projectors, commercial displays, digital signage, active LED, video walls, source switching, mounting, cabling, commissioning and support.

faqs.question: Which video brands can GPSPL support?
faqs.answer: GPSPL can support project-fit video systems including Sony, Lumens, HP Poly, Samsung, BenQ, Epson, Absen, ATEN and other technologies depending on the application.

faqs.question: How does GPSPL select a camera or display?
faqs.answer: GPSPL studies room size, lighting, viewing distance, participant count, camera coverage, presenter position, platform requirement, installation constraints and support expectations before recommending products.

faqs.question: Can GPSPL support video walls and active LED?
faqs.answer: Yes. GPSPL can support video walls, active LED display systems, controllers, mounting, source routing, calibration, commissioning and post-installation support.

faqs.question: Can video technologies be integrated with audio and control?
faqs.answer: Yes. Video is planned with audio, microphones, room control, source switching, connectivity and conferencing platforms so the complete room works as one system.

faqs.question: Does GPSPL provide installation and AMC?
faqs.answer: Yes. GPSPL can provide installation, commissioning, user training, warranty guidance, preventive maintenance, AMC and upgrade support based on project scope.

faqs.question: Can GPSPL help before procurement?
faqs.answer: Yes. GPSPL can support product shortlisting, BOQ preparation, compatibility checks, RFQ support and procurement guidance before deployment.

cta.headline: Plan the Right Video Technology Stack Before You Buy
cta.subheading: Share your room type, camera needs, viewing distance, display or projection requirement, content sources and support expectations. GPSPL can help you select, supply, install and support the right video technologies.

mistakes.title: Weak Screen Brightness
mistakes.description: Buying low-nit commercial displays for sun-lit glass lobbies, causing washout visual output.

mistakes.title: No Latency Validation
mistakes.description: Routing AV-over-IP systems over non-managed switches, leading to voice-video synchronization lags.

mistakes.title: Failing Projector Throw
mistakes.description: Buying standard throw projectors for short classrooms, casting presenter shadows across the screen.

mistakes.title: Skipping Active Extenders
mistakes.description: Routing 4K signal sources without active fiber extenders, resulting in handshake drops.

comparison.title: Laser Projector Setup vs. Active LED Display Wall
comparison.description: Key differences for large-venue displays and lecture hall environments.

rows.label: Ambient Light Handling
rows.col1: Prone to washout in brightly lit rooms; requires dimming lights.
rows.col2: Vibrant display in direct sunlight/ambient light (600-1000+ nits brightness).

rows.label: Installation Space
rows.col1: Requires throw distance from ceiling mount to wall screen.
rows.col2: Flat mount directly onto the wall structure, saving ceiling/floor space.

rows.label: Shadow Obstruction
rows.col1: Presenters can block the projection beam, casting shadows.
rows.col2: Direct emission display, zero presenter shadow or glare issues.

rows.label: Total Cost of Ownership
rows.col1: Lower initial cost; periodic filter cleaning and alignment checks.
rows.col2: Higher initial cost; extremely low maintenance and 100,000h module life.
